title: Fetching in an Effect: the race condition

slides.text: Your fetch can show the wrong person 😱
slides.say: Fetching data in an effect looks simple. But it can show the wrong data. Here is how.

slides.text: Looks fine… until responses arrive out of order.
slides.say: This effect fetches a bio whenever the person changes. It looks fine.

slides.text: Pick Bob, then Taylor. Taylor's answer comes first, Bob's arrives last and wins.
slides.say: But pick Bob, then quickly Taylor. If Taylor's response arrives first and Bob's arrives last, Bob's bio overwrites Taylor's. Wrong person!

slides.text: Cleanup marks old requests as stale.
slides.say: The fix: an ignore flag. When person changes, the cleanup sets ignore to true, so the old response is simply ignored.

slides.text: You can't undo a request. Each render's Effect has its own ignore variable.
slides.say: You can't undo a network request. But each render's effect has its own ignore variable, so a stale response can't affect your app.

slides.text: Fetch in an Effect? Ignore stale answers. 🛡️
slides.say: Fetching in an effect? Always add cleanup that ignores stale responses.
